Alex Ferreira holds a Bachelor's degree in Construction Project Management and has over 25 years' experience across construction, engineering and project delivery. He is your contact for extension projects.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for my extension?
faqs.a: Rear extensions up to 45 m² may be exempt if they meet all the conditions, including a 12 m² limit on the upper floor of a semi-detached or terraced house and minimum distances from windows to the boundary. We check your house first, and a Section 5 declaration gives certainty.

faqs.q: Will you work with my architect?
faqs.a: Yes. We price and build from your architect's or designer's drawings and work with your design team. Phibsborough was built to Francesco Panzeri's design and Leixlip to NBK Architects' drawings.

faqs.q: We do not have a designer yet. Can you help?
faqs.a: Yes. We develop layouts, 3D views and planning and design drawings, and bring in an architect or engineer where the project needs one. Design is a paid service with a fixed fee quoted after the first meeting.

faqs.q: Do you do the structural design?
faqs.a: No. Structural design and calculations come from an external engineer. We build to the engineer's design and bring one in if you do not have one.

faqs.q: How is the price set out?
faqs.a: In a detailed written quotation based on the drawings, listing the work and what is included.

faqs.q: Do you work in my area?
faqs.a: We work within 50 km of Dunshaughlin, Co. Meath. That covers all of Dublin and towns in Meath, Kildare, Louth (such as Drogheda) and north Wicklow.

sections.title: The 45 m² rear extension exemption
paragraphs: It may be exempt if it meets every condition, including height limits relative to the house; we check your site first. For certainty, you can ask the council for a Section 5 declaration. This is a summary, not legal advice.
bullets: Rear extensions up to 45 m² in total may be exempt (up from 40 m²), counting any earlier extensions
Upper floor limited to 12 m² on a semi-detached or terraced house, and 20 m² on a detached house
Upper-floor extensions at least 2 m from a party boundary
Ground-floor windows at least 1 m from the boundary they face; upper-floor windows at least 8 m
At least 25 m² of rear garden kept, and the roof cannot be used as a balcony
An exempt extension up to 45 m² does not need a Commencement Notice, but Building Regulations still apply
The exemption applies to the main house only, so it cannot be used to extend a garden home
